question: Was the rev13 five-draw gear a QA-injected grant, or an explicit in-app local free-candidate mock draw; can rev91 30-clear be described as no-test-gear progression?

evidence.generator: GameEngine.swift:1203-1242 command is literally mockSummon; it consumes ticket_free, chooses catalog templates, and synthesizes AFFIX_POWER_TEST/AFFIX_VITALITY_TEST/AFFIX_GUARD_TEST (and Q4 LATENT_*_TEST), then returns MOCK_ONLY R3 test draw / candidate only.
evidence.clearReceiptStatus: The campaign clears are persisted encounter receipts in the save; this audit does not identify a direct QAScenarios/fixture mutation on this run. The prior local summon path is nevertheless a test-overlay route.

judgment.accurateDescription: 30/30 is real local UI-dispatched campaign progression on the R420 candidate Release profile, with five free tickets spent through the visible in-app mock summon route. It is not a direct save/QA-scenario grant.
judgment.boundary: It is not evidence of a no-test-overlay/no-mock-gacha ordinary gear progression. Three items produced by rev13 mock draw remain equipped at rev91, including EQ_W_P2 (whose catalog entry has poison effects). Their precise marginal contribution to these wins is not isolated; do not assert they changed a win or quantify strength without combat comparison.
judgment.recommendation: If the acceptance claim requires no mock/test affix assistance, describe the existing 30 clears as candidate/mock-assisted, then perform only the needed replay evidence with owned non-mock alternatives (the rev91 inventory includes starter EQ_W_01 and EQ_S_01); do not erase or invalidate the original history.

limitations: This answers route/provenance, not whether mock affix IDs materially change combat stats.
The in-app route is local candidate functionality, not Apple StoreKit, production gacha, or approved monetization.
R443 remains interim; later challenge operations/final closure are outside this review.
